item.title: Experimental and Computational Investigation of Thermal Conductivity in Porous Silicon: Doping-Dependent Performance of Molecular Dynamics and Physics- Informed Neural Networks
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Pavlo Lishchuk, Lesia Chepela, Victoria Shevchenko, Mykola Borovoy, Vasyl Kuryliuk, Oleg Olikh
Porous silicon (pSi) is a highly promising material for nanoscale thermal management, but predicting its thermal conductivity remains challenging due to complex structure-property dependencies. In this work, we present a comprehensive multiscale investigation of heat transport in pSi, combining experimental gas-microphone photoacoustic (PA) measurements with atomistic Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations and continuum-level Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). Mesoporous pSi layers with porosities ranging from 48% to 75% were fabricated via electrochemical etching of highly doped p+-type silicon, and their effective thermal conductivity was experimentally determined. item.title: Physics-Coupled Task Allocation for Collaborative Robotic Welding of Dissimilar Steel Joints Using an α-Potential Game and a Physics-Informed Neural Network Surrogate
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 mohammad reza omidi
Collaborative robotic welding of dissimilar steel joints involves coupled decisions concerning task assignment, welding sequence, thermal interaction, energy consumption, and production time. Conventional distance-based allocation methods do not explicitly account for the fact that neighboring welding operations may modify the thermal state and mechanical response of subsequent operations. This study proposes a physics-coupled task-allocation framework in which collaborative welding robots are modelled as players of an α-potential game and the thermo-mechanical response is evaluated using a physics-informed neural-network (PINN) surrogate. item.title: Q-IDS Bench: Reproducible and Resource-Aware Evaluation of Quantum-Inspired Intrusion Detection Across Five Network and IoT Datasets
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Fuad Ibne Jashim Farhad, Dr MD Mamunur Rashid, Ali Shahidinejad
Very high IDS scores are frequently reported, but one ac curacy measure does not by itself show whether a detector will remain reliable under a different split, preprocess ing pipeline, or deployment budget. Q-IDS Bench exam ines this issue by benchmarking nine quantum-inspired intrusion-detection system (IDS) configurations on five datasets, all implemented on classical hardware. The data are divided into training, validation, and test sets before fitted preprocessing, and each experiment is repeated with five random seeds. Performance is assessed with weighted F1, AUPRC, MCC, false-positive rate, attack recall, and model-side inference latency. item.title: Counting magnetic flux quanta offers new way to measure photon numbers
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Researchers at AIST have directly observed magnetic flux quanta generated in a superconductor by photon absorption and demonstrated a new principle of photon detection that identifies the number of photons based on the number of these flux quanta.

item.title: Extreme temperature gradient drives substantial thermoelectric current in additive manufacturing
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Fengyuan Lin, Hui Chen, Yajing Sun, Haiou Yang, Meng Wang, Wentao Yan 等7位作者
Thermoelectric effects are commonly neglected in engineering alloys because their Seebeck coefficients are small. Here we show that this material-centred assumption fails under the extreme temperature gradients of additive manufacturing (AM). item.title: Multi-Dimensional Structural Fingerprinting for Quantitative Polymorph Comparison: A Comprehensive Topological Analysis of Sulfathiazole, Galunisertib and Aripiprazole Polymorphs
item.description:
